sn1.20:9.1: “Here, sir, I rose at the crack of dawn and went to the hot springs to bathe.
sn1.20:9.2: When I had bathed in the hot springs and emerged from the water I stood in one robe drying my limbs.
sn1.20:9.3: Then, sir, late at night, a glorious deity, lighting up the entire hot springs, went up to me, and, standing in the air, addressed me with this verse:
sn1.20:10.1: ‘Mendicant, you seek alms before you eat;
sn1.20:10.2: you don’t seek alms after eating.
sn1.20:10.3: But you should eat first, then seek alms:
sn1.20:10.4: don’t let the time pass you by.’
sn1.20:11.1: When this was said, sir, I replied to that deity in verse:
sn1.20:12.3: That’s why I seek alms before eating,
sn1.20:12.4: so that the time may not pass me by!’
sn1.20:13.1: Then, sir, that deity landed on the ground and said to me:
sn1.20:13.2: ‘You’ve gone forth while young, mendicant. With pristine black hair, you’re blessed with youth, in the prime of life, and you’ve never flirted with sensual pleasures.
sn1.20:13.4: Don’t give up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time.’
sn1.20:14.1: When this was said, sir, I said to that deity:
sn1.20:14.2: ‘I’m not, respectable sir, giving up what is apparent in the present to chase after what takes effect over time;
sn1.20:14.3: I’m giving up what takes effect over time, respectable sir, to chase after what is apparent in the present.
sn1.20:14.4: For the Buddha has said that sensual pleasures take effect over time, with much suffering and distress, and they’re all the more full of drawbacks.
sn1.20:14.5: But this teaching is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’
sn1.20:15.1: When this was said, sir, that deity said to me:
sn1.20:15.2: ‘But in what way, mendicant, has the Buddha said that sensual pleasures take effect over time, with much suffering and distress, and they’re all the more full of drawbacks?
sn1.20:15.3: And how is this teaching apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves?’
sn1.20:16.1: When this was said, sir, I said to that deity:
sn1.20:16.2: ‘I’m junior, respectable sir, recently gone forth, newly come to this teaching and training. I’m not able to explain this in detail.
sn1.20:16.3: But he, that Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, is staying near Rājagaha in the Hot Springs Monastery.
sn1.20:16.4: You should approach him and ask about this matter.
sn1.20:16.5: And you should remember it in line with the Buddha’s answer.’
sn1.20:17.1: When this was said, sir, that deity said to me:
sn1.20:17.2: ‘It’s not easy for us to approach the Buddha, as he is surrounded by other illustrious deities.
sn1.20:17.3: If you go to the Buddha and ask him about this matter, we’ll come along and listen to the teaching.’
sn1.20:28.5: The Garden of Delight chapter, the second.
sn1.20:29.1: The Garden of Delight, and Delight,
sn1.20:29.2: and There’s Nothing Like a Child;
sn1.20:29.4: Sleepiness and Sloth, and Hard to Do;
sn1.20:29.5: Conscience, Little Hut as the ninth,
sn1.20:29.6: and the tenth is called With Samiddhi.
